section_summary: This concluding section continues a secret intelligence report cataloguing the wartime information supplied to Japanese military attaché Makoto Onodera by German, Finnish, Swedish, Estonian, Polish, Hungarian and other European sources. It organizes reporting by target—especially the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union and Germany—and describes Finnish assistance in breaking foreign diplomatic and military codes. The final appendices identify personnel of the Japanese military-attaché offices in Stockholm and Helsinki, Japanese journalists and Legation and naval-attaché staff in Stockholm.

subfiles.title: Japanese Military Intelligence Activities in Europe: Sources, Target-Country Summary, Cryptanalysis and Personnel Appendices
subfiles.to: G-2, CINCAFPAC, Tokyo; TD-WDGS; Office of Naval Intelligence; Department of State; Central Intelligence Group; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Continuation and conclusion of a report on Onodera's European intelligence sources, the information they supplied, Finnish cryptanalytic cooperation and Japanese personnel in Stockholm and Helsinki.
subfiles.summary: Pages 78-93 complete tabular summaries of the German, Finnish, Swedish, Estonian, Polish and Hungarian sources that supplied Japan with military, political, economic and technical intelligence about the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union, Germany and other countries. Pages 93-94 describe Finnish success against American, British, Turkish, Soviet and other communications, including the changing weaknesses and security features of Soviet wartime codes. Pages 95-100 provide personnel and biographical appendices for the Japanese military-attaché offices in Stockholm and Helsinki, Japanese journalists and the Japanese Legation and naval-attaché office in Stockholm, ending with the report's distribution list.
